centralQuestion: Can Samsung FlexWash be represented as a composition of existing frozen functional contracts without distorting the diagnostic ontology?
executiveSummary: FlexWash is a dual-load wash topology, not a vocabulary problem. The lower wash compartment and shared infrastructure (drain, power, HMI, lower door lock, lower DD motor, lower-column heater faults) bind cleanly to front_load_washer functions without distorting the frozen graph. The upper compartment (independent motor, independent door/interlock DC4, upper-column fault codes) and cross-load behaviors (AC7 inter-PBA communication, SF system fault, dual-column diagnostic partition) cannot be represented on a single front_load_washer instance without collapsing compartment scope. Under the composition test model (LOWER FL instance + UPPER FL instance + shared power/HMI + integration boundary where required), the remaining unrepresentable behaviors all cluster at the integration/orchestration layer — not at ordinary washer component vocabulary. AIO precedent demonstrates that composition-by-reference can work, but required freezing a new integration function (integrated_laundry_orchestration) rather than forcing cross-mode behavior into front_load_washer. FlexWash has analogous integration evidence (AC7, SF, shared inlet/drain across PBAs) but only one witness manual (WV55M9600) and no frozen dual-load orchestration contract. Evidence does not support option A under a strict reading (existing frozen contracts only). Evidence supports option B tendency if an integration abstraction must be frozen before normalization can proceed. Option C applies to cross-manufacturer corroboration and some upper-compartment measurement specs (deferred in extraction).

aioComparison.rationale: AIO proves composition-by-reference works when a new integration function is properly fit/frozen — it does not authorize copying integrated_laundry_orchestration to FlexWash. Dual-wash-drum integration is a different functional boundary (interload comm, dual partition, not wash-dry orchestration). AIO required 2 witnesses before freeze; FlexWash has 1.
